mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.2% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE has been above 5.2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in UNRATE indicates a monetary policy response to labor market weakness, which typically precedes a 20-day S&P 500 decline due to reduced corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a 20-day return regression over the last 5 years, or the negative return pattern fails in more than 50% of interaction events.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST above 1050 thousand units), rising home construction activity signals strong consumer spending and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1050 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past 3 months indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where RSAFS has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5%, it triggers a monetary policy tightening expectation that increases equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a supply chain disruption regime (INDPRO growth rate below 0.5% for 3 months), reduced industrial output leads to higher inflation and slower economic growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth rate is below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months.
